 Coventry v Fulham (15:00 BST) 
 Sophie Brown 
BBC Sport 
 Image source, Getty Images Coventry City's two-game winning run may have come to an end against Tottenham on Monday but there will still be plenty of optimism going into today's meeting with Fulham.
 Frank Lampard's side had a tough start on their return to the top flight, losing four games in a row without scoring.
 But three of those fixtures were against the current top three (away at Manchester City and Arsenal , and at home to Brighton ). Having now got points and goals on the board, their next two matches are against clubs currently in the relegation zone.
 Coventry centre-back Bobby Thomas has been one of their standout players in this campaign. After 16 clearances against Newcastle – the second-most by a player in a match this season – he made a game-high seven at Tottenham, and tops the Premier League rankings for that metric.
 But there wasn't much he could do against Spurs, where unusually all three of their goals came from outside the box, meaning the Sky Blues have conceded more than twice as many such goals as any other team in the Premier League this season.

 Arsenal v Everton (15:00 BST)

BBC Sport Arsenal reporter at Emirates Stadium 
 The rain is really coming down here at the Emirates. 
 The Arsenal players are warming up on the far side of the pitch. 
 Just next to them are a group of supporters who have tickets in a hospitality area. 
 They are very expensive tickets and they have all been kitted out in ponchos or with club umbrellas to watch the warm-up.

 'Room to improve' published at 14:38 BST 14:38 BST 
 FT: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City captain Ruben Dias, speaking to TNT Sports: "Frustrating, felt like we fought a lot. First 10-15 minutes of the first half we took our time to get into the game.
 "They changed the way they set up so we took time to adapt. But we fought, we had chances and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions - very efficient. Room to improve, we need to do better.
 "It is what it is. Whatever happens we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction. The second one was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. Not our day but we keep moving forward.
 "I felt like we were dangerous on many occasions, even if the finish wasn't there we arrived in dangerous places but not able to play. A word of appreciation to the boys because we kept fighting to the end."
 On facing Brighton twice in a week next: "A top team, another one. A different way to play so we'll make the adaptation then focus on ourselves that's the main thing - our spirit, our will to win."

 Arsenal fear Saka could be out for two months published at 14:37 BST 14:37 BST 
 Arsenal v Everton (15:00 BST) 
 Image source, Getty Images Arsenal will be without key winger Bukayo Saka today, of course, and the club fear he could miss a minimum of six weeks with the quadriceps injury he sustained in their Champions League tie against Bayern Munich.
 The 25-year-old will undergo an MRI scan on Friday afternoon to better assess the problem, which forced him off in Wednesday's 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena.
 Fluid around the affected muscle has made diagnosing the injury difficult, but club medics are estimating, after early examinations, Saka will miss a minimum of six weeks and it could be even longer.
 If those early concerns are realised, he will miss a clutch of key games for the Gunners, as well as England's forthcoming Uefa Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.
 "We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists," said Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta.
 "When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, and is restricted to movement; it is not a good sign. Let's be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment.
 "He's got another MRI as there was quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was quite difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more tomorrow."

 FT: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa striker Nicolas Jackson, speaking to TNT Sports: "It was incredible, we got the win which is the most important thing. Man City are a strong team, the league leaders. Hopefully now we forget about this one and focus on the next one."
 On causing havoc for the Man City defenders: "I'm happy to do it every time, I will continue working for the team and the coach and that's most important for me."
 On settling quickly at Aston Villa having worked with Unai Emery before: "It's not easy but easier because of the coach. We have an incredible dressing room with the players and the coach."

 Image source, Press Association Image caption, Nicolas Jackson has scored seven goals in 11 appearances for Aston Villa since joining from Chelsea in August
 By Phil Cartwright BBC Sport journalist Nicolas Jackson's well-taken double for Aston Villa ended Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season. 
 City had taken maximum points from their first seven league games but Enzo Maresca's team fell to their first defeat against a Villa side who have an exceptional recent record against them.
 This victory was Villa's fifth in their past seven meetings against City, a fourth successive win against them at Villa Park and came on the fourth anniversary of Unai Emery's appointment as Villa boss.
 Villa captain John McGinn pounced on a poor touch by City defender Marc Guehi to play in Jackson, who turned inside Elliot Anderson and finished high into the net past Gianluigi Donnarumma for the hosts' opener.
 Iliman Ndiaye hit the post as the visitors pressed for an equaliser, which eventually arrived early in the second period when Erling Haaland climbed highest to nod in Ndiaye's cross from the right.
 However, parity lasted only eight minutes as Jackson met substitute Ibrahim Mbaye's low cross with a first-time shot that went in underneath Donnarumma's left hand.
 Another goalbound Haaland header late on was cleared to safety by Ian Maatsen as Villa registered their first home league win of the season.
 City's lead at the Premier League summit remains at three points, with second-placed Arsenal hosting Everton at 15:00 BST, while Villa have climbed into the top half of the table.
 Jackson stars with two goals - player ratings for Aston Villa v Man City 
 Published 14 minutes ago 
 Have your say on Aston Villa's performance 
 What did you make of Manchester City's display? 
 Villa's reshaped squad finding form 
 Villa lost their first two league games of the season but recovered well, taking 11 points from their subsequent six Premier League matches.
 The turnover of players during the summer months has been well documented and, on recent evidence, their reshaped squad has the potential to continue the club's success under Emery.
 Four of their summer arrivals started the win against City and all played an important role - most notably Jackson, who has netted seven times in 11 games in league and cup for Villa.
 The former Chelsea forward took his two goals extremely well. They were Villa's only two shots on target in the game but he, along with Johan Manzambi, posed a threat on the break during spells of City pressure.
 One counter-attack just before half-time led to Guehi pulling Jackson down on the edge of the box and receiving a yellow card.
 At the other end, Joao Gomes broke up play on several occasions in tandem with fellow midfielder Boubacar Kamara.
 Goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made first-half saves from Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov, plus another crucial stop from Josko Gvardiol just after Haaland's equaliser, which proved pivotal.
 Soon after, Mbaye - another of Villa's recent arrivals - made an immediate impact from the bench with the cross for Jackson to tuck home what proved to be the home side's winner.
 More to follow.
